title: Private Health Insurance (National Joint Replacement Register Levy) Amendment (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2022
short_title: Private Health Insurance (National Joint Replacement Register Levy) Amendment (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would update terminology in the national joint replacement register levy legislation to match proposed changes to private health insurance rules for medical devices.
It would replace references to joint replacement prostheses with device terminology, update related definitions and correct a mistaken reference to a ministerial determination.
Its operation would depend on the relevant part of the companion medical device legislation commencing, with commencement no earlier than its own royal assent.
changes: Sponsor provisions would refer to devices instead of prostheses.
Rules allowing classes of joint replacements to be included or excluded would use medical device terminology.
The supplementary levy day definition would point to section 8A rather than section 6.
summary.affected: Sponsors of joint replacement devices subject to the national joint replacement register levy would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Several bills were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration, including amendments to private health insurance, therapeutic goods, and export control legislation.

speeches.speaker: Julian Leeser
speeches.brief: The Coalition argued for three bills to modernise the Prostheses List, which sets minimum insurers’ payments for surgical implants, and allocated $22 million over four years to lower medical device costs and improve private health insurance affordability. The speaker criticised the Albanese Labor government for lacking transparency by leaving key details like eligibility criteria and cost recovery specifications to unsighted subordinate legislation.

speeches.speaker: Mike Freelander
speeches.brief: The package of three bills modernises the Private Health Insurance Prostheses List to improve transparency and reduce costs for implantable medical devices, with hip replacements costing over $4,000 in Australia compared to under $2,000 in the UK and New Zealand. The reforms aim to lower private health insurance premiums by reducing device costs and updating cost recovery arrangements.
